title: Existence and uniqueness of the section tensor-pullback representative comparison
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and let $f:X\to Y$ be any morphism of schemes, with their small pro-etale sites small relative to the coefficient universe [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use the section-module categories $\mathcal S_T$, cochain localization $Q_T:C(\mathcal S_T)\to D(\mathcal S_T)$, conjugate derived tensor $\mathsf T_T$, and signed direct-sum total $\operatorname{Tot}_T$ of [def-pd-section-derived-tensor-data], for $T=X,Y$. Complexes are arbitrary unbounded integer-indexed cochain complexes; retain independent site object, site morphism, and coefficient universes, and assume the chosen derived categories exist. Let $q_T$ be the unique natural transformation specified in [lem-pd-section-tensor-representatives-exists-unique]. Let $F=f^*_{\mathrm{sec}}:\mathcal S_Y\to\mathcal S_X$ be the fixed exact ordinary module pullback with its specified adjunction-mate oplax tensor map $\delta_{M,N}:F(M\otimes N)\to FM\otimes FN$ of [def-pd-proetale-section-module-functors]. Write $F_c$ for termwise pullback, $LF$ for its exact localization, and $\epsilon_A:LF(Q_YA)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_X(F_cA)$ for its fixed factor isomorphism of [def-pd-section-derived-tensor-data]. Define $b_{P,Q}:F_c\operatorname{Tot}_Y(P,Q)\to\operatorname{Tot}_X(F_cP,F_cQ)$ by the preserved-coproduct comparison followed on the degree-$(p,q)$ summand by $\delta_{P^p,Q^q}$ and the canonical summand inclusion. Both totals use the differential $d_P\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_Q$.

There exists exactly one natural isomorphism of bifunctors
$$d_f:LF\circ\mathsf T_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathsf T_X\circ(LF\times LF)$$
with the following equation for every pair of section-module complexes $P,Q$:
$$Q_X(b_{P,Q})\circ\epsilon_{\operatorname{Tot}_Y(P,Q)}\circ LF(q_{Y;P,Q})
=q_{X;F_cP,F_cQ}\circ\mathsf T_X(\epsilon_P,\epsilon_Q)\circ d_{f;Q_YP,Q_YQ}.$$
Both sides are arrows from $LF(\mathsf T_Y(Q_YP,Q_YQ))$ to $Q_X\operatorname{Tot}_X(F_cP,F_cQ)$. The equation is required for all complex pairs, without a K-flatness, termwise flatness, or boundedness hypothesis.

proof.text: Uncurry mapBifunctorComparisonNatTrans for the specified ordinary oplax pullback map. Since that ordinary comparison is strong and pullback preserves coproducts, its signed total is a natural isomorphism. Its components are exactly totalPullComparison: the explicit totalTensor object equalities contribute identities.

proof.text: Use the internal functorial flat resolution of the inverse image of any section complex. Internal pullback preserves flat objects and the colimits used by that resolution, so both the resolution complex and its pulled-back complex are categorical K-flat. Transfer those tests through internal_section_tensor_comparison and transfer the second along the termwise pullComparison. Apply the section equivalence to the resolution map, then its counit, to obtain a quasi-isomorphism from a section complex K-flat both before and after pullback.

proof.text: On resolving pairs the specified qTensor maps are invertible, for both the source and the pulled-back pair. Their restricted inverses provide the model isomorphisms for tensorComparisonDescent. Exact localization factors are invertible on every complex, including total tensors. The signed total pullback isomorphism supplies the chain comparison, giving the unique derived comparison on resolving pairs.

source.place: Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product; resolving-pair descent and naturality calculation.

proof.text: Both sides of the required all-complex equation are natural transformations. Choose resolving quasi-isomorphisms A to P and B to Q. The derived source bifunctor sends the pair to an isomorphism because localization inverts both resolution maps. Naturality and equality on A,B permit cancellation of this source map, proving the equation on arbitrary P,Q. Uniqueness restricts an alternate all-complex equation to resolving pairs and cancels the invertible qTensor factors. No ordinary total-tensor image of a resolution map is inverted.

theorem tensorPullComparison_existsUnique {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    ∃! d : tensor Λ Y ⋙ derivedPullback Λ f ≅
        ((derivedPullback Λ f).prod (derivedPullback Λ f)) ⋙ tensor Λ X,
      TensorPullRepresentativeCondition Λ f d
